title: Simulation of a counter-loop body
statement: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $S$ and $\Gamma$ be types with decidable equality, and let $e:\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\hookrightarrow\Gamma$ be an embedding. Let $M$ be a deterministic Turing machine over $\Gamma$ with $k$ work tapes and state set $S$, and choose $a\in S$ and an optional exit state $\mathrm{exit}\in\mathrm{Option}(S)$. For an input word $x$, let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ with state $a$, and let $ct:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathrm{Option}(\Gamma)$ and $cp\in\mathbb{Z}$ specify the contents and head position of an added counter tape; choose $t,\mathrm{width}\in\mathbb{N}$ with $0<t$. Suppose that for every integer time $u$ with $0<u<t$, the run of $M$ from $c$ has a state $s$ satisfying $s\ne a$ and $\mathrm{exit}\ne\mathrm{some}(s)$. Then after $t$ steps, the counter-loop machine formed from $M$, $e$, $a$, and $\mathrm{exit}$ has the configuration obtained by embedding the configuration of $M$ after $t$ steps and redirecting its optional state: states equal to $a$ enter the decrement phase, states equal to $\mathrm{exit}$ enter the escape phase, and other states remain in the body phase; the added counter tape and its head position are still $ct$ and $cp$. Moreover, at every time $u<t$ the counter-loop machine is in neither its done nor escape state, its added counter head lies in $[cp-1,cp+\mathrm{width}]$ at every time $u\le t$, and there is some $u\le t$ at which all its original $k$ work-tape head positions agree with those of $M$ after $u$ steps from $c$.

$M$ is a $k$-work-tape machine over $\Gamma$ with state set $S$
$c$ is a configuration on input $x$ and has state $a$
